planning.heading: Planning: {{period}}
planning.intro: This month hasn't happened yet — real transactions above are just whatever's already pre-scheduled (e.g. a known future installment). Everything below is expected, not real, split by how sure we can be: committed (recurring bills, debts' own schedule) vs assumed (your card-spend goal/average, and any known future card charge with no history yet).
planning.cardRoomLeft: Card room left after known charges
planning.inOutGlance: In vs out at a glance
planning.inOutGlanceIntro: The three tables below, as two bars — does expected income cover what's going out, and how much of the outgoing is still assumption rather than commitment.
planning.expectedByCategoryIntro: Committed and assumed expenses rolled up by category, using each bill's own category assignment.
planning.committedExpensesTooltip: Planned payments and debts' own known repayment schedule — essentially certain
planning.assumedExpensesTooltip: Your card-spend goal/average, plus any known future card charge with no transaction history yet — an estimate, not a fact
planning.outlookIntro: The same expected in − expected out, for every projected month — so {{period}} reads in context ("is this month unusually tight, or is that just what's coming") instead of floating alone. The outlined bar is the month you're planning; click any other to jump to it.

chart.moneyInOutTitle: Money in vs out per month
chart.moneyInOutIntro: Excludes transfers between your own accounts and money moved to/from investments — that's still your money, not spend or income. For future months there's no real cash flow yet, so the faded segments show what's expected instead, in two confidence tiers — the darker "committed" tier is real recurring bills and debts' own schedule; the lighter "assumed" tier is your card-spend goal/average standing in for spend that hasn't happened. The gold line is your 3-month rolling net average — the actual direction, without one unusually expensive or light month reading as a trend. Click a bar to jump to that month.
chart.balanceOverTimeIntro: Cash on hand plus current investment holdings (past months are a slight underestimate for investments — we only get today's value from Pluggy, not a historical one, so accrued yield isn't reflected). Click a point to jump to that month.
chart.topCategoriesIntro: A pie can't show whether a category is creeping up — this can. Your {{count}} biggest expense categories this period, each as its own line. Future months use categorized recurring bills (real transactions don't exist yet), so a line doesn't just flatline to zero once it crosses into the future. Click a point to jump to that month.
chart.cardSpendIntroPerMonth: What you charged on each card each month — separate from bank cash flow above, so a card purchase and the bill payment that later settles it aren't counted twice. Click a bar to jump to that month.
chart.cardSpendIntroThisMonth: What you charged on each card this month — separate from bank cash flow above, so a card purchase and the bill payment that later settles it aren't counted twice.
chart.cardSpendByCardExtra: Real pre-scheduled amounts (e.g. an installment already dated) are solid. On top, two fainter tiers: "committed" is a recurring bill with real history behind it, "assumed" is a known future charge with none yet (e.g. a planned trip) — or, for the current month, however much of your card-spend goal hasn't posted yet, so a month still in progress doesn't read as a cliff-drop next to a finished one.
chart.cardSpendByCategoryExtra: Stacked by category instead of by card — where the money actually went, month by month.
chart.inOutIncludedNote: Card purchases count individually and the bill payment that settles them is left out, so nothing is double-counted — which is also why totals here can run higher than the bank-only Money in / out figures above.
chart.inOutExcludedNote: Bank transactions only — credit card activity is excluded.
chart.clickSliceHint: Click a slice or legend entry to see the transactions behind it.
